newsitem.title: TURKEY: West Turkey phone lines cut by anchoring vessel.
newsitem.headline: West Turkey phone lines cut by anchoring vessel.

text.p: Telephone communications in Turkey's western region have been severely disrupted after an anchoring Panamanian cargo vessel broke off a main undersea fibre optic cable off the Dardanelles strait, officials said on Wednesday.
"The ship broke an 18,000-way fibre optic cable line under the sea near the Dardanelles," said Fethi Ercan, regional director of Turk Telekom, the state telephone company.

He told reporters the Iolcos Pioneer, which was carrying 153,000 tonnes of U.S. coal to Constanza, Romania, was put under a "precautionary seizure" status until the damage to the cables was fully assessed.
The accident occured on Tuesday morning, when the vessel tried to anchor off after a fault in its engines but later drifted at anchor because of strait currents.
Istanbul maritime officials said the vessel sailed through the Sea of Marmara to the Bosphorus strait after repairing the engine fault but they stopped it there to fine it.
"If the ship agrees to pay the fine, which I cannot disclose now, the precautionary seizure status will be lifted and it can sail on its way," an Istanbul port official told Reuters.
He said the vessel is now anchored off Ahirkapi, at the southbound end of the Bosphorus.
Ercan said the cable break has caused telephone lines in the major port city of Izmir and other towns to be disrupted since Tuesday morning.
"The break in the cables stopped almost all mobile and normal telephone communication of western Turkey with Europe and Japan," Ercan said.
"Telekom is losing about 80 billion lira ($561,000) a day from the damage," he said.
He said a French ship, equipped to mend such faults, was coming to Turkey and predicted that the lines would be repaired by the weekend.
